facts.text: Haus, Sherony and Gabler combined US pedestrian crash data with theoretical automatic-braking systems across a grid of time-to-collision triggers and latencies to estimate crash avoidance and fatality-risk reduction for each combination. The retrospective simulation was published in Traffic Injury Prevention in 2019 and was peer-reviewed; the evidence is on-road only.
facts.quote: Haus, Sherony and Gabler (Traffic Injury Prevention, 2019) combined US pedestrian crash data with theoretical automatic-braking systems over a grid of time-to-collision triggers and latencies

facts.text: A 2025 arXiv study analyzed a V2X-enhanced partial-brake plus automatic-braking system against real-world road-crash reconstructions. The study was a preprint and was not peer-reviewed.
facts.quote: A 2025 arXiv study analyzed a V2X-enhanced partial-brake plus automatic-braking system against real-world crash reconstructions (preprint, not peer-reviewed).

facts.text: In a 2015 on-road grade-aware simulation study, a braking trigger based on surface condition but not grade worked at 0% grade but resulted in collisions at 11% and 17% grade.
facts.quote: a trigger based on surface condition but not grade worked at 0% grade and collided at 11% and 17%

facts.text: In the 2015 on-road grade-aware study, including grade shifted full-brake initiation earlier and avoided the modeled collisions.
facts.quote: including grade shifted full-brake initiation earlier and avoided the modeled collisions.

facts.text: The 2015 on-road grade-aware study illustrates that a braking trigger can appear correct on a level proving ground yet be structurally wrong on grade.
facts.quote: a trigger can look correct on a level proving ground and be structurally wrong on grade.

facts.text: The 2026 ESV round robin found tool disagreements of 0.033 s and 0.314 m in a brake-only test despite prescribing a 1.0 s trigger, 0.2 s delay, 0.4 s build-up, 1 g and µ = 0.9. Baseline differences were larger before harmonization; this is on-road evidence.
facts.quote: even with a prescribed 1.0 s trigger, 0.2 s delay, 0.4 s build-up, 1 g and µ = 0.9, tools disagreed by 0.033 s and 0.314 m in the brake-only test, with larger baseline differences before harmonization.

facts.text: The simulator itself needs verification: a common scenario description does not guarantee equivalent initial conditions, reference points, time-to-collision definitions, tire behavior or actuator implementation. This lesson is supported by the on-road 2026 ESV round robin.
facts.quote: The simulator itself needs verification: a common scenario description does not guarantee equivalent initial conditions, reference points, time-to-collision definitions, tire behavior or actuator implementation.

facts.text: NIOSH stopping-distance modeling is identified as the closest public off-road precedent for simulation used to tune thresholds before field testing.
facts.quote: NIOSH stopping-distance modeling (the closest public precedent).

facts.text: NIOSH built a dynamic stopping model because proximity systems designed for slow crawler mining machines were being considered for faster rubber-tired underground haulage, raising concern that existing detection zones might not cover stopping distance.
facts.quote: NIOSH built a dynamic model because proximity systems designed around slow crawler mining machines were being considered for faster rubber-tired underground haulage, raising concern that existing detection zones might not cover the stopping distance.

facts.text: The NIOSH underground-haulage stopping model allowed changes in brake force, grade, initial speed, lag and rolling resistance.
facts.quote: The model allowed changes in brake force, grade, initial speed, lag and rolling resistance.

facts.text: NIOSH stopping-model sensitivity work showed that more brake force shortened predicted stopping distance.
facts.quote: more brake force shortened predicted stopping distance

facts.text: NIOSH stopping-model sensitivity work showed that initial speed strongly affected stopping distance.
facts.quote: initial speed strongly affected distance

facts.text: NIOSH stopping-model sensitivity work showed that brake-system lag changed stopping distance even at underground speeds.
facts.quote: brake-system lag changed stopping distance even at underground speeds

facts.text: NIOSH stopping-model sensitivity work showed that grade materially changed stopping outcomes.
facts.quote: grade materially changed outcomes

facts.text: For some parameter combinations in the NIOSH underground-haulage stopping model, downhill force exceeded braking capability and the machine did not stop.
facts.quote: for some combinations the downhill force exceeded braking capability and the machine did not stop.

facts.text: The authors of the NIOSH stopping-model work envisioned reducing field tests after model validation but did not present the model as field-validated. The work was presented at ASME IMECE in November 2018.
facts.quote: The authors envisioned using the model to reduce field tests after validation, and did not present it as field-validated (ASME IMECE, November 2018).

facts.text: Companion NIOSH work in 2016 collected data for 145 underground haulage machines in five categories and statistically selected representative parameter sets.
facts.quote: The companion NIOSH work collected data for 145 underground haulage machines in five categories and statistically selected representative parameter sets (2016).

facts.text: ISO 21815-3 embeds model-based thinking in its risk-zone framework through informative annex examples for configuring collision-system parameters from machine stopping performance.
facts.quote: ISO 21815-3 embeds model-based thinking in its risk-zone framework: its informative annexes include examples for configuring collision-system parameters from machine stopping performance

facts.text: Using a correlated stopping model to configure risk zones is aligned with ISO 21815-3 rather than an alternative to the standard.
facts.quote: using a correlated stopping model to configure risk zones is aligned with the standard rather than an alternative to it.

facts.text: A 2019 excavator virtual-reality evaluation tested time-to-collision-based safe, warning and emergency-braking modes in a "sticking" scenario.
facts.quote: Excavator virtual-reality evaluation* of time-to-collision-based safe, warning and emergency-braking modes in a "sticking" scenario (2019).

facts.text: The 2019 excavator virtual-reality evaluation was simulation-only and reported no field comparison.
facts.quote: Simulation only; no field comparison reported.

facts.text: University of Pretoria kinematic-sampling collision prediction reported simulation-only initial results in Springer Lecture Notes in Mechanical Engineering in October 2024.
facts.quote: University of Pretoria kinematic-sampling collision prediction* (Springer Lecture Notes in Mechanical Engineering, October 2024). Simulation-only initial results.

facts.text: Griffith University used Monte Carlo simulation plus a field demonstration of a Doppler-radar system in 2005 and reported detection of light vehicles at 75 m.
facts.quote: Griffith University (2005)* used Monte Carlo simulation plus field demonstration of a Doppler-radar system and reported 75 m detection of light vehicles.

facts.text: The 2005 Griffith University Doppler-radar work was a detection study, not a brake-threshold study.
facts.quote: It is a detection study, not a brake-threshold study.

facts.text: NIOSH continuous-miner intelligent proximity zones were designed using retrospective analysis of MSHA fatality reports from 1984 to 2014 rather than physics simulation.
facts.quote: NIOSH continuous-miner intelligent proximity zones* were designed from retrospective analysis of MSHA fatality reports (1984 to 2014) rather than physics simulation

facts.text: In the NIOSH continuous-miner intelligent-proximity-zone study, 32 of 39 fatalities with published investigation reports, or 82%, were judged preventable under the zone configurations studied.
